title: Four Heroes Church
paragraphs: “Hmm, that sounds fine. We can stop by the Four Heroes Church first.”
At Ren’s words, Father and the others nodded.
“You’ll be amazed when you see it. The Four Heroes Church headquarters is one of the most famous landmarks in the world,” Éclair said.
Soon, the grand structure of the Four Heroes Church came into view. It reminded me of the massive churches I had seen while traveling overseas before being summoned.
“Huh? This isn’t a castle?”
“It’s certainly big, but isn’t the castle that even larger building over there in the distance?”
“Yeah, the Melromarc castle doesn’t even compare to that one.”
Rather than the church, Father and the others were more focused on Faubrey’s castle.
“Still, this church is huge… It looks like one of those buildings you see in overseas travel programs on TV.”
“I get what you mean. I didn’t expect a structure this massive… Hm?”
Ren seemed to have noticed something. Following his gaze, I saw a stained glass window.
“What’s that glowing light in the stained glass?”
“Ah, that is said to be proof that the heroes have been summoned and are alive.”
“There’s something like that?”
“As long as that light continues to shine, it is considered a beacon of hope, symbolizing the world’s safety.”
Father and the others leaned out of the carriage, staring at the glow. If I recall correctly, in the first world, Father wasn’t very interested in it.
“Huh…”
“Enough talk. Let’s head inside.”
Ren stepped down from the carriage and started walking toward the church.
“Yeah. We need to go prove our status.”
Father followed suit. Naturally, Assistant and Mole trailed along with him. Itsuki and I also followed.
“What about the carriage?”
“There’s a parking area nearby. Leave it there.”
“Got it!”

Sakura-chan and the others drove the carriage to the parking area Éclair pointed out. Since there were actual cars around, calling it a parking lot didn’t feel strange at all. We waited for Sakura-chan and the others to return before heading into the Four Heroes Church headquarters.
“Stone-paved stairs… Normally, I wouldn’t pay much attention to them, but they feel strangely imposing,” Father remarked as he looked up at the church while climbing the stairs.
That’s true. This kind of stone pavement might only be found in Faubrey. Though, to be fair, stone roads exist in every country.
“For a Japanese person, this might feel like a fresh experience. In games, you pass by places like this all the time without thinking much about them.”
“I never found them odd in VR.”
“Well, Ren, you basically played VR games that were practically another world already. Maybe you’ve even been to a place like this in-game?”
“The name was different, but… yeah. I even remember roughly how the interior is structured.”
“I also recognize this place from game screens.”
“So there really are buildings that match our game knowledge.”
“Though I’ve learned the hard way not to rely on it too much.”
With that conversation, we climbed the stone stairs and passed through the large open doors into the building.
“Pardon our intrusion,” Éclair addressed a nun-like pig standing at the entrance.
“Buuh!”
The nun-like pig, bowing politely, turned its eyes toward us. Since it was a pig, I had no idea what it was saying. Still, for a pig, it gave off an air of refinement.
“The Four Holy Heroes summoned from Melromarc have arrived. We request an audience with the church officials.”
Éclair also bowed before responding.
“Eclair-san? Should we do something?”
“If you have any way to prove you are heroes, please do so. It will make things go smoother.”
“Like this?”
Ren raised his sword and repeatedly changed the weapon’s appearance. Weapon transformation was indeed one way to prove he was a hero. Although, I’d heard there were some weapons with similar effects.
“Using a skill would work too, but that could be dangerous.”
“No, this is fine. There are other ways to verify it with equipment, so making a strong first impression should be enough.”
“I’ve heard there are cases where similar transformations can be replicated.”
I had heard that too, and the weapon the previous pope wielded was a prime example of that. Just then, a priest emerged from the back. Since he was human, I could understand his words.
“…I have confirmed it. I will take you to the High Priest immediately.”

The nun-like pig hurried into the depths of the building. In its place, the priest guided us inside. Passing through the chapel visible from the entrance, we were led to a reception room deeper inside. We waited there for about thirty minutes.

Then, the leader of the Four Heroes Church? An elderly man approached us. He had a very different presence from the pope of the Three Heroes Church—a well-built man. The Three Heroes Church’s pope always had a suspiciously constant smile, while this one had a warm, genial expression, as if naturally spreading joy to those around him. Not that he was fat. His ornate robes made him look bulkier than he was.
“Oh!”
Suddenly, he tripped and flailed about in a panic.
“Ah, ah! Four Holy Heroes, welcome! You have traveled far to reach Faubrey. Yes, yes.”
…Is it just me, or does he seem incredibly shady? Something about him felt familiar.
“Do you have a relative who’s a monster merchant?”
“Hm? No, I have no such relatives…”
Was it just my imagination? Or was he hiding it? I decided to assume he was a distant relative.
Surely, he wasn’t from the main family. Perhaps the monster merchant was from a branch family. Maybe he didn’t even know about it himself.
“Now then, in order to verify that you are indeed the Four Holy Heroes, please take a look at this. It may be a bit dazzling.”

Saying this, the High Priest of the Four Heroes Church directed an ornament attached to his staff—something resembling a pinwheel—toward us. Immediately, our weapons glowed and emitted light toward that pinwheel.
“I have confirmed it. There is no doubt that you are the Four Holy Heroes.”
“Oh, so that’s a tool to verify heroes?”
“Yes… Over the ages, since the time of legend, there have always been imposters claiming to be heroes…”
“So, there are tools like this as well.”
Ren stared intently at the pinwheel. This was my first time coming here… But I do recall seeing this High Priest several times at the castle.

He was likely involved in various matters during the incident with Takt as well. I also remember him showing up when Fiancée inherited the throne. Father had refused an audience with him, though… Father never liked dealing with religion.
“We plan to request an audience at the castle. Does this verify our identities sufficiently?”
“Yes, there is no issue.”
The High Priest then captured an image of us with a crystal.
“With this, you should have no trouble entering the castle. Yes, yes.”
“I see… Then, there’s nothing more we need here, is there?”
At that moment, the High Priest stepped forward.
“Please wait, heroes. There is something I would like you to see. Might I ask for a bit of your time?”
“Hm? What is it?”

“There exists an inscription left behind by a past hero and a prophet who foretold the world’s end. The prophecy states that when the next heroes arrive, they must be allowed to view it. It has been passed down through generations.”
“Ah… wasn’t that mentioned when we first got summoned to this world?”

Was there something like that? I tried to recall. …Oh! That’s right. That fool explained it back then. I only remember how arrogant he was and how cliché the whole thing sounded. Come to think of it, wasn’t that supposed to be the reason we were summoned?

So, this is the inscription left by the prophet who made that prediction… If I think about it, leaving behind such a prophecy so long ago is quite impressive, isn’t it? Perhaps it is worth checking out.
“I see… but even so—”
“We haven’t fully mastered this world’s language or magic yet.”

That’s true. I have been teaching Father and the others, but they have yet to fully grasp magic. At the very least, I had them learn basic spells using magic orbs from a magic shop to help them get a feel for it.

For now, I am teaching them this world’s language using the Melromarc script that I translated. They can probably read simple magic texts, but we haven’t purchased any magic books yet. I should have bought some while we were still in Melromarc.
